findings.issue: In 来るべきだった ('should have come', regret) the verb is read くる. きたるべき is the fossilized literary attributive ('forthcoming', e.g. 来るべき時代) and does not fit this predicative pattern; the record's own token note says 'dictionary form of 来る (くる)'.
findings.current: きのうきたるべきだったのに。
findings.suggested: きのうくるべきだったのに。

findings.issue: Reading of 来る wrong in context: should be くる (plain 'to come' + べきだった), not the literary きたる. The token's own note states the base is 来る (くる).
Romaji carries the same wrong reading 'kitaru' for 来る; in this sentence it is 'kuru'. (Separate from the already-known punctuation issue.)
後から出てくる means the best APPEARS LATER (is yet to come). 'The best is behind' reads in English as 'the best is in the past', reversing the meaning. pt and lit_en render it correctly.
findings.suggested: The best is yet to come.

findings.issue: すばらしい means 'wonderful/splendid', not 'fresh and clean'; the en invents qualities absent from the jp and contradicts the record's own lit_en and token gloss ('wonderful'). 'In the mountain' is also unidiomatic.
findings.current: The air in the mountain is fresh and clean.

findings.issue: Token list opens with two stray null-glossed sub-tokens 早(はや) and め(め) placed BEFORE 昨夜, duplicating the correct token 早め that follows; concatenated surfaces no longer reconstruct the sentence (早め昨夜早めに…).
findings.current: tokens: [早(はや), め(め), 昨夜, 早め, に, ねる, …]
findings.suggested: Delete the two stray leading tokens 早 and め; keep the single 早め token in its position after 昨夜.

findings.issue: Token list opens with two stray null-glossed sub-tokens 運転(うんてん) and 手(しゅ) placed BEFORE 昨日, duplicating the correct token 運転手 later; concatenated surfaces no longer reconstruct the sentence (運転手昨日ここに…).
findings.current: tokens: [運転(うんてん), 手(しゅ), 昨日, ここ, に, 着い, た, 運転手, …]
findings.suggested: Delete the two stray leading tokens 運転 and 手; keep the single 運転手 token in its sentence position.

findings.issue: 'In the mountain' is unidiomatic English for 山の中で (it suggests inside the mountain); idiomatic is 'in the mountains'.
findings.current: Have you ever seen a bear in the mountain?
findings.suggested: Have you ever seen a bear in the mountains?

findings.issue: 'I mean,' has no counterpart in the jp (no discourse marker like つまり/だって); it implies preceding discourse that does not exist. Rest of the translation is fine.
findings.current: I mean, I was spellbound the whole time.
findings.suggested: I was spellbound the whole time.

findings.issue: Subject 'he' contradicts the record's en and pt, which use 'you' (the natural reading of this のに reproach); jp has no overt subject, so the record should be internally consistent.
findings.current: He should have come yesterday, but (he didn't).
findings.suggested: You should have come yesterday, but (you didn't).
